This toner is packaged in plastic bottle with a drip top dispenser. The product info says it's fragrance free and it doesn't smell of anything to me. The serum is clear and the texture is quite runny. It's well suited for application with a cotton ball or pad. It absorbs very quickly and well. It isn't sticky, oily or greasy. When it dries it doesn't actually feel like you've applied anything, but my skin does feel moisturised. I've been using it nightly for just over two months on washed and dried skin (normal to dry).

avis.texte: I must confess that I don't usually use a toner in my skincare routine. I usually double-cleanse, firstly with a cream cleanser and then with a Vitamin C Micellar Water. However, I have recently become aware of the benefits of Korean skin care products and own several Mixsoon-branded products, which I am very happy with. I suffer from rosacea, and while my post-menopausal skin has always been sensitive, it is now also very dry. Therefore, I am always cautious when trying new products. However, I was keen to try this because it claims to calm redness and irritation and is suitable for all skin types, though I am unsure whether it can help with acne. Also, it is fragrance-free and only four ingredients are listed on the sales page: Water, Butylene Glycol, 1,2-Hexanediol and Houttuynia Cordata Extract. However, on my packaging, the only ingredient listed is "Houttuynia Cordata Extact" [sic], and this differs from the image shown, which is for Galactomyces toner, not HeartLeaf toner. The bottle contains 300ml of Mixsoon HeartLeaf toner, which doesn't have any obvious scent. However, the consistency is very watery, and there is no pump dispenser or perforated inner plug to help with dispensing the product effectively. This is a packaging oversight: if the toner is accidentally knocked over, most of the product will be wasted. avis.titre: A solid, minimalist staple for maintenance and skin prep ...
avis.texte: I bought this for my wife. It took her almost the entire month to truly make up her mind about this heavily hyped social media favorite. While it didn't deliver dramatic "miracle" results for her cheek inflammation, it proved its worth as a dependable, ultra-gentle SOS relief layer. It functions beautifully as a skin-prepping "booster" that helps subsequent skincare products absorb much better. The Performance Breakdowns Texture & Application: True to its claims, this is a lightweight, water-based, and non-sticky formula. It spreads beautifully, absorbs rapidly, and leaves absolutely no greasy residue. It feels incredibly refreshing upon application, making it a joy to use. Soothing & Sensitivity: The brand promises a "minimalist formula" free from unnecessary additives and fragrances, and my sensitive skin can confirm this. When my skin suffered a sudden, strange reaction to another product, this toner (paired only with a ceramide cream) provided immediate, non-irritating calm. It didn't actively cure the reaction, but it safely hydrated and soothed the skin without exacerbating the issue. Hydration & Layering: Because the texture is so watery, it layers beautifully and works excellently for sensitive or combination skin. However, as a standalone hydrator, it is very light. If you have dry skin—or are using it during a cold, dry winter—you will definitely need to follow up with a much richer moisturizer. Longevity & Value: A little goes a long way.
